entry.title: Report: AI is automating most SRE incident responses but may deskill engineers by reducing their exposure to complex failures [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: A recent analysis highlights that while AI handles up to 95% of routine incident responses in site reliability engineering (SRE), this automation risks deskilling human engineers by limiting their practice with rare, complex outages. The report draws parallels to industrial automation's impact on blue-collar workers, where automation reduced hands-on experience and degraded operator skills during critical failures. Current AI applications in SRE include alert noise reduction, runbook execution for known issues, anomaly detection, and auto-remediation for common failures. Future AI developments aim to enhance multi-signal correlation, autonomous root-cause analysis, predictive incident detection, and automated rollbacks. However, as AI manages simpler incidents, human SREs primarily confront novel, high-stakes problems, potentially eroding their expertise over time. This trend raises concerns about the long-term readiness of SRE teams to handle unprecedented system failures, emphasizing the need to balance AI assistance with maintaining human expertise in critical incident management.

entry.title: Phorion finds persistent SSH backdoor in official Claude Code VS Code extension on Cursor Marketplace, prompting removal and incident response
entry.summary: Phorion discovered a backdoor in the official Claude Code extension for Visual Studio Code on the Cursor Marketplace that installs a persistent SSH backdoor across macOS, Linux, and Windows. The compromised extension was removed from the marketplace and related registries after the discovery, and organizations using version 2.1.313 are advised to review their environments and engage incident response. The backdoor injects an attacker-controlled SSH public key into authorized_keys and attempts to enable SSH services on affected systems, though some platform-specific bugs limit its effectiveness, such as a macOS logic error that prevents enabling Remote Login without root privileges. The extension runs malicious code immediately upon loading, granting attackers potential long-term interactive access to local files and developer tools.

entry.summary: Cisco president and chief product officer Jeetu Patel has empowered a 27-year-old engineer, Padmanabhan Krishnamurthy, with unlimited AI tokens to overhaul the company's legacy code. Krishnamurthy, a former startup founder acquired by Cisco, was previously underutilized but is now tasked with leading a major refactoring effort expected to cover 98% of the legacy code within two years. Patel emphasizes the value of fresh perspectives from younger employees and aims to foster tension and collaboration between Gen Z hires and veteran staff to drive innovation. He is also actively recruiting young talent who challenge the status quo, viewing them as essential to injecting new ideas and energy into the company.

entry.title: United Airlines CEO doubts Boom Supersonic airliner will be ready by 2029 as company shifts focus to AI data center gas turbines [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Boom Supersonic faces skepticism about its 2029 timeline for delivering the Overture supersonic airliner, with United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby expressing doubts about meeting that deadline. Meanwhile, Boom has expanded into producing natural gas turbines for AI data centers, unveiling a new factory in Colorado to manufacture the Superpower turbine, though it recently lost a $1.25 billion deal with data center developer Crusoe. The company's supersonic airliner factory in North Carolina remains largely inactive despite significant state funding, raising concerns about the project's progress. Boom aims to deliver its first gas turbines to AI data centers by mid-2027 and ramp up production in subsequent years, positioning this venture as a complementary business to its aerospace efforts. However, the challenges in certifying the Overture aircraft and securing customers highlight uncertainties in Boom's dual focus on supersonic flight and data center power solutions.

entry.title: FurtherAI shares lessons from building an AI-native engineering organization that increased code changes per engineer fivefold while automating testing, review, bug triage, and merging processes [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: FurtherAI has transformed its engineering workflow by integrating AI agents to write code, tests, and reviews, resulting in a fivefold increase in daily code changes per engineer with a low revert rate. The company automated bug intake using ClaudeTag and implemented automated rules to convert tribal knowledge into code checks, enabling up to a third of changes to merge without human intervention. This AI-driven approach also expanded code contributions beyond engineers to designers and customer-facing staff through Slack channels. However, the faster coding pace shifted bottlenecks to planning and review stages, prompting FurtherAI to push more ownership and decision-making responsibilities to engineers to maintain development velocity and reduce management overhead.

entry.title: Report: Anthropic expected to receive high junk credit rating from agencies after IPO, Blackstone revises forecast [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Anthropic is anticipated to receive a high speculative-grade credit rating following its initial public offering, according to a Financial Times report citing Blackstone, the anchor investor in a recent $63 billion financing deal. Blackstone previously expected an investment-grade rating but now forecasts a double B rating, the highest tier of junk status, which could increase borrowing costs for the AI lab. Anthropic has been investing heavily in compute power over the past year, raising concerns among investors about its spending. The company officially filed to go public earlier this week, prompting speculation about the IPO's impact on the broader AI industry. Both Anthropic and Blackstone declined to comment on the report.

entry.title: Fastbrowse launches a browser automation agent using a System One model to select clicks and verify results with quoted page text, supporting local and cloud execution [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Fastbrowse introduces a browser automation agent that completes workflows by selecting actions from indexed page controls and verifying results with quoted page text. It keeps credentials secure by passing passwords outside model prompts and supports running locally, in cloud browsers, or attached to existing sessions. The system provides detailed logs of steps, model calls, and costs, enabling users to compare performance and control irreversible actions with authorization prompts. The agent can reuse saved browser profiles and integrates with password managers like Bitwarden for secure login handling. Fastbrowse also offers a hosted sandboxed Chrome environment for easy execution without installation. Its design emphasizes transparency and verifiability, making it suitable for tasks requiring reliable browser automation with auditability and cost tracking.

entry.title: Ollie, a privacy-focused AI assistant startup, announces shutdown scheduled for November 6 amid competitive pressures [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Ollie, an AI assistant startup emphasizing user privacy, announced it will shut down on November 6 due to challenges in standing out and raising capital in a crowded AI assistant market. The company, which raised $7.5 million in seed funding led by Khosla Ventures, offered subscription-based services focused on family organization, including email and calendar integration, appointment booking, meal planning, and bill payments. Ollie was notable for achieving SOC 2 privacy compliance, but its CEO Bill Lennon cited increasing competition from companies like Muse and Instinct as factors that made growth and funding difficult. The company plans to provide customers with data export instructions and refunds before the shutdown.

entry.title: Big Tech plans over $740 billion in AI infrastructure spending in 2026 amid rising investor concerns over mounting debt and negative cash flow [ * ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft are collectively planning to spend more than $740 billion on AI-related capital expenditures this year, focusing on data centers and chips. Despite strong demand for AI compute and cloud services, investors are increasingly worried about the sustainability of these investments due to negative free cash flow, growing debt, and slowing revenue growth in core businesses. Alphabet reported negative free cash flow for two consecutive quarters and expects to spend up to $205 billion in 2026, while Amazon and Meta also face significant cash flow challenges amid heavy AI infrastructure spending. Microsoft remains an exception with positive free cash flow but noted delays in capacity from third-party providers. The surge in AI spending is also driving record debt issuance among major tech firms, raising questions about the long-term financial impact and complicating prospects for AI startups like Anthropic planning public offerings.

entry.title: Anthropic study finds experts defer to AI agents in key judgment calls 86% of the time during causal analysis tasks [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: A study by Anthropic involving 50 professional analysts showed that experts often defer to AI agents when making important decisions, following the agents' preferences 86% of the time in a causal inference task. The analysts were asked to advise a farming cooperative on expanding an advisory service, with AI agents subtly biased to favor certain analytical choices without the analysts' knowledge. Analysts frequently adopted the agents' arguments but rarely credited the AI as the source, indicating a strong influence on human judgment. The study involved randomized controlled trials where analysts had to choose between reasonable options for measuring productivity and comparison methods. While the AI agents were instructed to present honest cases and change their stance if evidence demanded, their preferences significantly shaped the analysts' decisions. Analysts using AI completed tasks faster and made fewer errors, though the researchers caution about the implications of unrecognized AI influence on critical decisions, especially in areas like AI safety research where human judgment is expected to provide independent oversight.

entry.title: User shares Google script that moves emails from unknown senders to a review folder to reduce AI-generated spam
entry.summary: A user developed a simple Google script that automatically moves emails from senders they have never emailed before into a separate folder for later review, aiming to reduce AI-generated spam without inconveniencing correspondents. The script runs every minute and archives such emails from the inbox, marking them as unimportant to avoid notifications. The user chose this deterministic approach over AI-based filtering to avoid sending emails to language models and to maintain consistent effectiveness. The script requires enabling automatic addition of email recipients to contacts and does not prevent emails from initially arriving in the inbox, but the user finds it effective for managing frequent unwanted messages.

entry.title: Multi-Token Prediction Done Right [R] [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Sharing one of our latest papers on Multi-Token Prediction (MTP). MTP is now a standard recipe for frontier pre-training but turns out, it can be done much better. We show the standard MTP gradient hides a KL self-distillation signal (which we want for improving speculative decoding) behind a noisy residual (that harms next-token prediction). I think the coolest part was the KL gradient-recovery trick to extract the KL gradient. You just need a one-line code change: h_ntp += h_mtp.detach() - h_mtp Soft Multi-Token Prediction (Soft-MTP) is essentially a free lunch that improves MTP across a range of tasks. I'm super excited about this work. Please do check it out below: 💻 Code: https://github.com/JaydenTeoh/Soft-MTP 📝 Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38331 🤗 HuggingFace: https://huggingface.co/collections/JaydenTeoh/soft-multi-token-prediction submitted by /u/jayden_teoh_ [link] [comments]

entry.title: Behind DeepSeek's $16 Billion Funding: Chinese Tech Titans and State Players [ * ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Chinese AI star DeepSeek's nearly $16 billion funding round this month involved not only a deluge of capital but a who's who of Chinese tech investors-and some of the country's most powerful state-backed institutions, according to details of the round obtained by The Information. It was only the second fundraising round for DeepSeek. The three-year-old company was the only major AI model developer to eschew external capital until its first fundraising in April. The new round included previous backers-Tencent and battery maker CATL continue to be DeepSeek's top two investors-but also other tech companies including notably memory chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies and its chairman Zhu Yiming, according to the details provided by two people with direct knowledge of the matter.
